title: Quality control: inspect, correct and hand over with pride

say: Quality control: inspect, correct, and hand over with pride.
This is the video for module five of Fashion Finishing and Quality Control.

Most makers check their work from memory, quickly, at the end of a long day. That is when faults slip through. Professionals use a written routine: the same points, in the same order, in good light, for every garment.

panel.heading: Quality control is a system, not a feeling
items: Same points, same order, every garment
Fix the cause, not just the fault
A handover that protects your name

say: The written record also protects you if a client later complains. Then you fix the cause of each fault, and finish with a handover that protects your reputation.

panel.heading: Quality control is a system, not a feeling
items: Same points, same order, every garment
Fix the cause, not just the fault
A handover that protects your name

say: Work outside to inside, top to bottom, so you never skip an area. First on the hanger: does it hang straight? Then the collar, shoulders, sleeves, and closures.

panel.heading: Outside to inside, top to bottom

say: Check pattern matching at the seams, the seams themselves, topstitching, the hem, and every bead and motif.

panel.heading: Outside to inside, top to bottom

say: Then inside out: finished edges, a free-hanging lining, trimmed threads and no chalk marks. Last, the measurements.

panel.heading: Outside to inside, top to bottom

say: A spec sheet lists the key finished measurements, and a tolerance is how far each may differ and still pass. For example, Amaka in Enugu's spec says bust 96, waist 80, hip 104 and length 110 cm, each plus or minus 1 cm.

panel.heading: Amaka checks a dress against its spec
items: Let hem down 1.5 cm, rehem narrow
panel.rule: A spec sheet lists finished measurements, each with a tolerance.

say: She measures flat and doubles. The bust is 97 cm, 1 cm over, which passes. Waist and hip also pass.

panel.heading: Amaka checks a dress against its spec
items: Let hem down 1.5 cm, rehem narrow
panel.rule: A spec sheet lists finished measurements, each with a tolerance.

say: The length is 108.5 cm, 1.5 cm short. That fails. She had turned up 3 cm, so she lets the hem down 1.5 cm and rehems with a narrow finish, before handover.

panel.heading: Amaka checks a dress against its spec
items: Let hem down 1.5 cm, rehem narrow
panel.rule: A spec sheet lists finished measurements, each with a tolerance.

say: A critical fault makes the garment unsafe: a broken needle left inside, or a loose small button on a baby's garment that could be swallowed. Critical faults are never accepted.
Count pins and needles before and after each job, and run a magnet over children's garments before handover.

panel.heading: How serious is each fault?

cards.d: Unsafe: a broken needle inside, a sharp edge, a loose small button on baby wear.
The client would be unhappy: a seam opening, a sticking zip, an uneven hem.
A small flaw that does not affect use, like one untrimmed thread inside.

say: A major fault would make the client unhappy, like a seam opening or a sticking zip. Fix it before handover.

panel.heading: How serious is each fault?

cards.d: Unsafe: a broken needle inside, a sharp edge, a loose small button on baby wear.
The client would be unhappy: a seam opening, a sticking zip, an uneven hem.
A small flaw that does not affect use, like one untrimmed thread inside.

say: A minor fault, like one untrimmed thread inside, is fixed whenever possible and recorded. For small batches, inspect every piece.

panel.heading: How serious is each fault?

cards.d: Unsafe: a broken needle inside, a sharp edge, a loose small button on baby wear.
The client would be unhappy: a seam opening, a sticking zip, an uneven hem.
A small flaw that does not affect use, like one untrimmed thread inside.

say: For example, Hauwa in Kaduna logs every fault for a month: 36 faults in 40 garments. Puckered seams are 14 of them, about 39 percent.

panel.heading: Hauwa asks why, and fixes the method
items: Why? Needle not changed, nobody responsible
New routine: puckered seams drop to 4

say: She asks why. Most are on one machine. Why? Its needle has not been changed for weeks. Why? No one is responsible for changing needles.

panel.heading: Hauwa asks why, and fixes the method
items: Why? Needle not changed, nobody responsible
New routine: puckered seams drop to 4

say: So she makes a routine: a new needle at the start of every new fabric type, written on a card on the machine. The next month, puckered seams drop to 4.
Keep asking why until you reach a cause you can change.

panel.heading: Hauwa asks why, and fixes the method
items: Why? Needle not changed, nobody responsible
New routine: puckered seams drop to 4
panel.rule: Correcting fixes today. Changing the method fixes every garment after.

say: Give every client a care card with the five basic symbols. The washtub is washing, and a hand in it means hand wash. The triangle is bleaching, and the square is drying.

panel.heading: The five basic care symbols
items: Washtub: washing; hand means hand wash
Iron: one, two or three dots for heat

say: The iron shows heat: one dot is low, three dots high. The circle is for the dry cleaner.
For example, Ijeoma in Asaba's card for a beaded lace blouse says hand wash in cool water, do not bleach, dry flat in the shade, and iron on low, from the inside, never on the beads.

panel.heading: The five basic care symbols
items: Washtub: washing; hand means hand wash
Iron: one, two or three dots for heat

say: Test the iron on a hidden seam allowance, and press through a press cloth on dark, shiny or beaded fabrics. Press, lift and move. Hang it to cool completely before packing.

panel.heading: Press, pack and hand over safely
items: Test heat; press through a press cloth

say: Put tissue in the sleeves and bodice, use a garment bag, and add the care card and a spare button.

panel.heading: Press, pack and hand over safely
items: Test heat; press through a press cloth

say: Ask her to try it on, and show her the closures and care card. Fake transfer screenshots are a known scam, so check the credit in your own banking app before you hand over the garment.

panel.heading: Press, pack and hand over safely
items: Test heat; press through a press cloth
panel.rule: Confirm payment in your own banking app. Never trust a screenshot.

say: To remember. Inspect in a fixed, written order. Measure against a spec sheet with tolerances. Never accept a critical fault. Ask why until you find a cause you can change. And hand over with a care card, after confirming payment in your own app.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Inspect in a fixed, written order
Measure against a spec with tolerances
Ask why until you find the cause

say: Now inspect one finished garment with the 12-point check and a spec sheet. Start a fault log for your last five garments. And build a handover kit with a care card and a follow-up message.
Continue with the lessons below.
